Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mhspcarpi (development version)

  • plot_treatment_effect() is removed; plotting moved to the web calculator. treatment_effect_curve() returns the curves for custom figures. graphics and grDevices are no longer imported.
  • The vignette is written in Quarto, and the README is shorter.
  • The web calculator moved to its own repository, https://github.com/wfukuokaya/mhspcarpi-app, which builds it from a pinned commit of this package. run_app() and mhspc_app() are removed, and shiny, bslib, htmltools, svglite, and shinylive are no longer suggested. The lower-level functions the calculator calls are exported and documented in ?"app-api".
  • Web calculator: now runs in Safari and in every browser on an iPhone or iPad (all of which use WebKit). R in WebAssembly ran out of stack there while building the page, computing the results, and drawing the plot. The page is rendered once with its deepest parts pre-rendered, the inputs and estimates are computed in one reactive, outputs return early instead of calling shiny::req(), and the effect plot is drawn as inline SVG with svglite, with hover and tap handled in the browser. The header gradient is picked in the browser. Checked with Playwright WebKit in iPhone emulation.
  • The loading screen text is shorter, and startup errors are shown on it.
  • Plots space the x-axis labels every 25% or 50% when the plot is too narrow for every 20%.
  • Web calculator: a loading screen with a progress bar replaces Shinylive’s faint loading indicator, which looked like a blank page on phones during the first visit. The page downloads the files R needs at startup while measuring progress, then starts Shinylive, which reads them from the browser cache (tools/loading/).
  • Calculator: the treatment-effect plot keeps a 4:3 shape as the window resizes, between 320 and 560 pixels tall, instead of a fixed 300 pixels.
  • Calculator: the hazard ratio for death, with its 95% CI, is shown beside the absolute treatment effects; the 2 risks and the 3 treatment effects now take one row each.
  • Plot labels have a thin white outline instead of a white box, and the “This patient” label is placed above or below the curve, whichever keeps it closer to the marker without crossing the curve.

mhspcarpi 0.1.0

  • Model version 261002-raw-rcs replaces 260803-raw-rcs. Its linear-predictor center matches the baseline hazards, which raises predicted risks; the example patient in the tests moves from 53% to 62%.
  • First version: baseline risk, treatment effects across baseline risk, input checks, plotting, and a Shiny calculator exportable with Shinylive. Model version 260803-raw-rcs.
  • A synthetic-cohort check (data-raw/synthetic_cohort_check.R) runs the analysis export code on simulated trials; the package reproduces rms predictions to 1e-9. It showed that the exported linear-predictor center must match survival::coxph(), which uses 0 as the reference for 0/1 and factor columns. With the rms center, predicted risks were too low (34% versus 45% observed in the simulation). The model specification built from the 260803 export has this problem; it is fixed in 261002_script.R and checked by data-raw/remote_golden_cases.R.
  • treatment_effect_curve() returns the pooled effect curves for custom figures and tables.
  • example_patients provides 6 synthetic patients spanning the range of baseline risk, and model_inputs() gains a definition column.
  • Calculator: a note for every input on obtaining the value in routine care (timing relative to androgen deprivation therapy, conventional imaging versus PSMA PET, laboratory methods, and upper caps), notes that close on a click outside them, hemoglobin in mmol/L and alkaline phosphatase and lactate dehydrogenase in microkatal per liter, the risk of death with an ARPI plus ADT shown beside the baseline risk, inputs filled from the query string, and a model-specification panel with the coefficients.
  • A “Get started” vignette.
  • Calculator design: a brand file (_brand.yml) following Quarto’s default HTML look (system sans-serif fonts on a white page) with the JAMA color palette, applied through generated CSS variables; the title in white on a layered radial gradient, chosen at random on each page load.
  • The calculator and the treatment-effect plot describe the comparator as ADT alone, for use in practice without placebo; the About panel explains that it corresponds to the placebo plus ADT arms of the trials.
  • The treatment-effect plot shows baseline risk from 0% to 100%, with the curve covering the range observed in the trials.
